best_for: Bitcoin holders who want to keep their own keys on their own computer, without downloading the whole blockchain, and who are willing to check a GPG signature.

points.title: Fast because it skips the full chain
points.text: Electrum checks your own transactions with SPV and asks public servers for the rest, so it opens in seconds instead of syncing hundreds of gigabytes. The trade-off is that it leans on those servers to see the network.

points.title: Your keys stay on your machine
points.text: Private keys are encrypted and kept on your computer, and a recovery phrase can rebuild the wallet if the computer dies. Keys can be exported to other Bitcoin wallets. The app is free and open source under the MIT license.

points.title: Cold storage and shared wallets
points.text: You can keep keys on an offline computer and use a watch-only wallet on the online one. Multisig splits spending rights across several wallets. Hardware wallets work through plugins.

points.title: Fakes are the main risk
points.text: The project says to download only from electrum.org and to verify each file's GPG signature against ThomasV's key. It does not publish hashes on purpose. Anyone offering private 'Electrum support' is likely a scammer.

points.title: The Flatpak is not on the official list
points.text: The download page lists Windows, Mac, AppImage, source and Android builds, and no Flatpak. The Flathub package carries the Electrum developers' name but Flathub does not mark it as verified, so it cannot be checked with the project's signatures the same way.

points.title: System needs
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later on x64; this listing keeps 34 Windows versions. The Mac build needs macOS 11 or later and is one universal app. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.
